meta.title: GSL-297 — Web control plane feature-complete · verifier-297 audit (run 02)
meta.run_scope: Adversarial re-audit of the six tasks GSL-298..303 landed on the branch. Formed per-task verdicts BEFORE reading docs/reports/verifications/GSL-297/runs/01/, then diffed. Re-ran typecheck + bun test + lab-smoke on both branch and pinned-main.

verdict.summary: Independent verification concurs with runs/01's substantive claims. All six tasks GSL-298..303 land the code, docs, and evidence they promised, with one or two strict-reading Jira-vs-shipped deviations openly named in the dev history. Gates are green: tsc-core clean, tsc-web clean, bun test 191/0, .claude/settings.json byte-diff vs main = 0. Lab-smoke adjudication: branch = 562 pass / 0 fail; pinned main-wt at 56f57d1 = 406 pass / 160 fail — every single main-wt fail is in the 'chronicler: the T3 regenerator (GSL-86)' section, i.e. the OLDER docs/lab/site/*.html files pinned at 56f57d1 don't satisfy the T3 self-re-grade contract. NONE of the main-wt fails is introduced by this branch. The '6 fails' the builder saw earlier (556/6) were transient shared-tree state — the live chronicler has since re-rendered the html and they resolved. Two MINOR findings (both honestly acknowledged in the dossier / dev history, none blocking): GSL-298 shipped a flat snapshot layout while Jira asked for a date-subdir layout; GSL-300 provided shim-direct evidence rather than the real-subordinate-session leg the Jira description asked for. Score softened from a perfect 100 to 96 to reflect one minor-but-real Jira-vs-ship deviation (GSL-300) and one strict-reading spec deviation (GSL-298 layout) — both are non-blocking and would be reasonable follow-ups, not gate failures.

per_task_verdicts.title: Fleet live-values proof + flushPendingObservations bug fix
evidence_reviewed: apps/core/src/routes/internal.ts diff: `existing !== null && existing !== undefined` branch selector fix (Bun `.get()` returns null); per-row try/catch replacing `db.raw.transaction` wrapper; `core.tool_observed.flush_error` log on per-row failure.

tools/lab/tests/core-smoke.sh scenario 25b: POST tool-observed with fresh sid → sleep 2 s past debounce → sqlite3 SELECT WHERE session_id=<sid> must return `Read|42`. Proper regression fence for the fixed bug class.
assets/v6-agent-sessions-db.txt: post-fix DB row shows the fresh session_id landed with current_tool=Read, context_pct=42.
assets/v6-fleet-projection.json: /fleet projection includes the row.
per_task_verdicts.note: This was a verification-only task that uncovered a REAL LATENT BUG (silent INSERT-drop for first-time session_ids). The bug analysis is correct — verified by reading the code + Bun 1.3.x behavior: `db.query(...).get(...)` returns `null` when no row matches, not `undefined`. Removing the transaction wrapper is defensible (best-effort telemetry, per-row atomicity is enough), and per-row try/catch keeps one bad row from dropping the batch. Acceptable trade-off given the data domain.
